A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 60-page versions of the same survey, with matching sections, Table 1, Figures 1–2, and reference lists. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, despite a shared appendix pointer in Section 2.2.2.

before.justification: v1 presents a literature survey and taxonomy. Its benchmark statistics, performance examples, simulations, and user studies are attributed to cited work; no original empirical investigation is reported.

after.justification: v3 remains a literature survey without original empirical results. The added HealthBench description and multi-agent critiques explicitly concern other researchers' work.

M1.justification: The reviewed algorithms and methodological taxonomy remain unchanged. Neither version introduces a proposed model or algorithm; the new multi-agent recommendations describe future research priorities.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for its own training or evaluation. Section 2.2.2 adds HealthBench to the literature reviewed, without conducting an experiment on it.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. The added references do not introduce comparators into an experimental comparison.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol conducted by the survey is introduced or revised. HealthBench's conversation statistics, physician-developed rubrics, and subsets describe a cited benchmark rather than settings adopted for an experiment.

E4.justification: No new ablation, robustness test, or empirical case study is conducted. The added multi-agent failure discussion synthesizes cited critiques without presenting a new supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance reporting is introduced. HealthBench's handling of clinical uncertainty concerns response evaluation, not statistical uncertainty estimation by the survey.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the existing cited performance results remain unchanged. HealthBench is described without model scores, while the new multi-agent paragraph discusses limitations without adding concrete evaluation results.

T1.justification: No formal mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The additions are descriptive literature discussion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution claims: a task-oriented taxonomy, synthesis of applications and improvement methods, and organization of open challenges. The claimed scope and novelty are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3.2 adds specific multi-agent limitations involving role misassignment, communication overhead, error propagation, inadequate verification, and miscoordination or collusion, together with research priorities. Section 2.2.2 also adds an appraisal of HealthBench's alignment with clinical judgment.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the survey's resource-repository link. The HealthBench overview supplies no new implementation instructions or concrete access instructions.

R1.justification: Four references are added: HealthBench and multi-agent critiques by Han et al., Cemri et al., and Hammond et al. All earlier references are retained, and the positioning against previous surveys remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds two localized paragraphs and removes the stray SMILECHAT prefix and detached Ding et al. paper-title fragment from the healthcare and education openings. Section organization and nearly all remaining wording are unchanged.

P2.justification: Added prose and references produce local page reflow, including moving the jailbreak section opening from page 23 to page 24 and occupying more of page 35. Table 1 and Figures 1–2 retain their designs and placement, with citation renumbering in Figure 1.

improvement.justification: v3 improves critical balance by adding concrete multi-agent failure mechanisms and risks after v1's favorable summary in Section 3.3.2. The HealthBench overview updates healthcare coverage, and removing stray text improves readability. These are useful, localized gains; the central taxonomy and substantive analysis otherwise remain intact.
